newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end mostly lower.

text.p: Most U.S. stock index futures finished moderately lower in nervous trade before key payrolls data on Friday.
A Reuters poll of economists pegged an average jobs gain in February of 230,000, with a jobless rate ot 5.3 percent, hourly wages up 0.4 percent and a 34.6-hour workweek.

March Standard and Poor's 500 futures slipped through support at 802.00 and 800.00 -- levels where buy-stops fueled Wednesday's rally -- and touched a session low of 798.10 before stabilizing into the close. Traders eyed weak T-bonds and a sagging Nasdaq index.

One S&P 500 futures trader said the S&P 500 "was trying to hold in there," but noted the divergence between it, the Nasdaq and the Dow. The Dow remained more resilient in afternoon trade, while the March Nasdaq 100 index slid through key 860.00 to the lowest price since Monday.
Some traders also tied March S&Ps' decline to a corrective mood after the late Wednesday run into the 800.00 handle.

One S&P floor trader said the perception was growing that the Federal Reserve would raise short-term interest rates on March 25, and said players would closely watch payrolls data for signs of strength in the economy.
"I think they're going to raise rates and I think it's going to happen the 25th," the trader said. A credit tightening would yank March and June S&Ps back near the 760.00 handle, he said.
"That would be a pretty big event and take this market down for a week," the trader said. Should the Fed stand pat on monetary policy, he said S&P 500 futures would roar to fresh record highs.
Others noted a Reuters story suggesting the odds were likely for the Fed to tighten on March 25. That, coupled with a rise in January factory orders, kept buyers wary, they said.
U.S. January factory orders rose 2.5 percent with December revised to down 1.5 precent from down 1.3 percent.

At the close, March S&P 500s were off 3.65 points to 800.60, Nasdaq 100s eased 20.25 to 855.50, Value Line futures were down 1.45 point at 714.75, Nikkei 225 index futures fell 595.0 to 17,850.0 and Midcap 400s rose 1.20 points to 266.60.
